take:
In these 14 posts Obsidian is rarely a standalone note app; it is the memory layer for an AI agent: a vault, which is just a folder of markdown files, that Claude Code reads and writes. Claude Code is tagged in 7 of the 14. @chase.h.ai suggests running Claude Code inside a vault as a markdown-native assistant [ten Claude Code plugins](/e/DVryCC1jfi1), later calls the vault the memory system of an "agentic OS" [agentic OS blueprint](/e/DXYSxNLpIAY), and points to kepano/obsidian-skills, which the caption says was built by Obsidian's CEO [seven repos](/e/DUzg0n1jRK-). @cooper.simson's agent file tree links the whole folder structure to Obsidian and GitHub for version control [agent file tree](/e/Db7Vx2Hhf9c).

The second cluster is knowledge graphs. @tenfoldmarc runs the Graphify skill on a Claude folder, then opens that folder as an Obsidian vault [graph-memory skill](/e/DXAshxEDM5m), and @marc.kaz shows the same one-command graph landing in a vault [codebase graph](/e/DW1st4HDp9K). The 71.5x token-reduction figure in one caption is not backed by anything in the entries. @jens.heitmann pairs Obsidian with Karpathy's LLM-Wiki document and says any file system Claude Code can see would also work [second brain overhaul](/e/DXCu2p4EQe3). See the [Claude second brain guide](/guides/claude-second-brain).

Some push back. @jesserurka says most people copy the same basic template and builds a custom librarian agent for clients [client knowledge system](/e/DWo1P-KDpMf), while @jonathonmj claims a plain vault "doesn't fire neurons" and pitches his own product, which one commenter called "larp" [Neurolinked pitch](/e/DXh4_OkDNG3). A viral post about an Anthropic engineer's 8,893-node vault cites no source [viral vault](/e/DadGSQ7lNLX). The tag is incidental in some posts, such as a MemPalace memory demo [MemPalace](/e/DW1O6ZBEfDa) and a Loom-to-skills recipe [self-improving startup](/e/DYxDK5ixq07).

It suits Claude Code users who want context to survive between sessions. Beginners get @alex2learn's walkthrough: install Obsidian, create a vault folder, drop exported data into it [vault walkthrough](/e/DWoxW7pjjkH).
